toilettenpapier.name: Toilet paper
toilettenpapier.kanal: Toilet paper is made to fall apart in water within seconds. On its way to the treatment plant it breaks down into fine fibres.
toilettenpapier.hinweis: The cardboard tube in the middle goes into paper recycling.
toilettenpapier.pointe: The VIP among toilet guests – always on the guest list.

urin.name: Urine
urin.kanal: Urine is perfectly normal wastewater. The treatment plant uses bacteria to remove nitrogen and phosphorus.
urin.pointe: Pee is a regular – the treatment plant knows it by its first name.

kot.name: Poo
kot.kanal: That’s what the toilet was invented for. At the treatment plant bacteria break it down – the sludge even becomes biogas.
kot.pointe: Your poo ends up as electricity. Honestly!

erbrochenes.name: Vomit
erbrochenes.kanal: It can go down the toilet and is cleaned at the treatment plant like other wastewater.
erbrochenes.pointe: Not a nice moment – but the toilet is on your side.

feuchttuecher.name: Wet wipes
feuchttuecher.kanal: Wet wipes are made of tear-proof fleece and do not break down. At the pumping station they wind around the pump impellers and form thick ropes. The pump stops and has to be cut free by hand.
feuchttuecher.pointe: Wet wipes love pumps. Sadly, it’s not a healthy relationship.

feuchtes-klopapier.name: Moist toilet paper
feuchtes-klopapier.kanal: Despite the name, it isn’t toilet paper but a wet wipe. It stays strong in water and tangles in pumps and pipes.
feuchtes-klopapier.hinweis: Put a small bin with a lid next to the toilet – problem solved.
feuchtes-klopapier.pointe: Calls itself toilet paper, behaves like a rope.

spuelbar.name: “Flushable” wipes
spuelbar.kanal: “Flushable” only means: it slides through the toilet. It does not mean: it dissolves. In the sewer these wipes tangle in pumps too.
spuelbar.pointe: “Flushable” is about as honest as “I’ll tidy up in a minute”.

taschentuecher.name: Tissues
taschentuecher.kanal: Tissues are made “wet-strength” so they don’t tear when you blow your nose. That’s why they break down much more slowly in water than toilet paper.
taschentuecher.pointe: Holds tight when you blow your nose – and sadly in the sewer too.

kuechenrolle.name: Kitchen roll
kuechenrolle.kanal: Kitchen paper is especially tear-proof and absorbent. In the pipe it hardly breaks down and can form blockages together with fat.
kuechenrolle.wohinHinweis: Whether lightly soiled kitchen paper may go into the organic bin is decided by your local waste service.
kuechenrolle.pointe: Soaks up everything – except the pump’s will to work.

wattestaebchen.name: Cotton buds
wattestaebchen.kanal: The thin sticks often slip through the screen at the treatment plant. Then they end up in the sludge or even in the river and later on the beach.
wattestaebchen.pointe: Small, thin, sneaky – the ninja of toilet sinners.

wattepads.name: Cotton pads
wattepads.kanal: Cotton soaks up water, clumps together and gets caught in pipes and pumps.
wattepads.pointe: Fluffy and soft – until 100 of them block a pipe.

abschminktuecher.name: Make-up remover wipes
abschminktuecher.kanal: Make-up remover wipes are wet wipes – tear-proof, indestructible and a nightmare for every pump.
abschminktuecher.pointe: Make-up off, pump off. Not a good trade.

binden.name: Pads & panty liners
binden.kanal: Pads contain plastic and absorbent material. They swell up and block the pipe in your own house.
binden.hinweis: Wrap in paper or packaging and put in the bin.
binden.pointe: Soaks up 100 times more than the pipe can handle.

tampons.name: Tampons
tampons.kanal: Tampons swell to several times their size in water. The string catches easily and forms ropes with other fibres.
tampons.pointe: In water the tampon turns into a puffed-up show-off.

menstruationstasse.name: Menstrual cup contents
menstruationstasse.kanal: The blood is normal wastewater and can go down the toilet. The cup itself, of course, not – it gets washed and reused.
menstruationstasse.pointe: Contents: welcome. Cup: please stay outside.

kondome.name: Condoms
kondome.kanal: Latex doesn’t break down. Condoms wrap around pump parts or float all the way to the treatment plant.
kondome.hinweis: Wrap in a tissue and put in the bin.
kondome.pointe: Reliable protection – just not for the pump.

windeln.name: Nappies
windeln.kanal: Nappies contain super-absorbent material that soaks up many times its weight in water. So a nappy becomes a plug that seals the pipe.
windeln.hinweis: You can tip the contents (poo) into the toilet first.
windeln.pointe: One nappy in the pipe – and suddenly the whole building has a problem.

zahnseide.name: Dental floss
zahnseide.kanal: Dental floss is plastic and never breaks down. It acts like a thread that collects hair and wipes into thick ropes.
zahnseide.pointe: The common thread of every pump failure.

haare.name: Hair
haare.kanal: Hair mats together with soap and fat in the trap and the pipes. A hairball quickly blocks the drain.
haare.hinweis: A strainer in the shower and sink drain reliably catches hair.
haare.pointe: In the drain, hair has really bad hair days.

rasierklingen.name: Razor blades
rasierklingen.kanal: Blades collect in pumping stations and screens. There they injure the people who clear blockages by hand.
rasierklingen.hinweis: Wrap the blade in cardboard or tape.
rasierklingen.pointe: Sharp in the bathroom, mean in the sewer.

kontaktlinsen.name: Contact lenses
kontaktlinsen.kanal: Contact lenses are plastic. At the treatment plant they get ground into microplastics and end up in sludge or water.
kontaktlinsen.hinweis: The blister pack goes into the yellow bag.
kontaktlinsen.pointe: They help you see clearly – but fish then see microplastics.

pflaster.name: Plasters & bandages
pflaster.kanal: Plasters stick, bandages are made of strong fabric. Neither breaks down – both get caught in pipes and pumps.

zahnpasta.name: Toothpaste (when brushing)
zahnpasta.kanal: The leftovers from brushing your teeth are perfectly normal wastewater. The treatment plant copes well with them.
zahnpasta.hinweis: The empty tube goes into the yellow bag.
zahnpasta.pointe: Spitting allowed – flushing the tube is not.

duschgel.name: Shower gel & shampoo
duschgel.kanal: That’s normal when showering. The surfactants are largely broken down at the treatment plant. Still, using less is better for the environment.
duschgel.hinweis: Please don’t pour away full bottles – use them up or give them away. Empty bottles go into the yellow bag.
duschgel.pointe: A dab will do – save the foam party for somewhere else.

nagellack.name: Nail polish & remover
nagellack.kanal: Nail polish and remover contain solvents. They harm the bacteria at the treatment plant that clean the wastewater.
nagellack.hinweis: Small dried-up remains in the bottle can go into general waste.
nagellack.pointe: The treatment plant bacteria aren’t into manicures.

bratfett.name: Frying fat & cooking fat
bratfett.kanal: Hot fat is liquid – in the cold sewer it turns solid. It sticks to the pipe walls and the pipes get narrower and narrower. It stinks, attracts rats and has to be flushed out at great cost.
bratfett.hinweis: Let it cool, pour it into a jar or tin with a lid, or soak it up with kitchen paper.
bratfett.pointe: In the sewer, chip fat becomes a fatberg. The rats say: thank you!

speiseoel.name: Cooking oil
speiseoel.kanal: Oil combines with other substances in the sewer to form sticky deposits. At the treatment plant it forms a layer that takes oxygen away from the cleaning bacteria.
speiseoel.wohinHinweis: Put it in a closed plastic bottle in the general waste. Some places have collection points for used cooking oil.
speiseoel.pointe: Oil and water don’t get along. They never have.

bratensosse.name: Gravy & fatty broth
bratensosse.kanal: The fat in it hardens in the sewer and forms deposits – just like frying fat.
bratensosse.hinweis: Let leftovers set in a container and put them in the general waste.
bratensosse.pointe: Tasty on the plate, sticky in the pipe.

speisereste.name: Food leftovers
speisereste.kanal: Food leftovers in the sewer are a feast for rats. They also form deposits and burden the treatment plant.
speisereste.wohinHinweis: Whether cooked leftovers may go into the organic bin is decided by your local waste service.
speisereste.pointe: The toilet isn’t a rat delivery service.

fleisch-fisch.name: Meat & fish leftovers
fleisch-fisch.kanal: Meat and fish rot in the sewer, stink and attract rats. Bones get stuck in pipe bends.
fleisch-fisch.wohinHinweis: Some waste services allow the organic bin – please check locally.
fleisch-fisch.pointe: Rats can’t read a menu – but they can smell one.

kaffeesatz.name: Coffee grounds
kaffeesatz.kanal: Coffee grounds settle like sand in pipes and traps. Together with fat they form a hard layer.
kaffeesatz.hinweis: Aluminium or plastic capsules go into the yellow bag.
kaffeesatz.pointe: Wakes you up – blocks the pipe up.

teebeutel.name: Tea bags
teebeutel.kanal: Tea bags don’t break down fast enough. Some even contain plastic fibres.
teebeutel.pointe: Let the tea brew – but not through the pipe.

obst-gemuese.name: Fruit & vegetable scraps
obst-gemuese.kanal: Peel and scraps settle in pipes and rot there. In compost they turn into valuable soil.
obst-gemuese.pointe: The organic bin makes soil – the pipe only makes trouble.

eierschalen.name: Eggshells
eierschalen.kanal: Bits of shell settle like gravel in pipes.
eierschalen.pointe: The hen worked so hard – into the compost!

reis-nudeln.name: Rice & pasta
reis-nudeln.kanal: Rice and pasta keep swelling in water and stick together. That’s how plugs form in the pipe.
reis-nudeln.wohinHinweis: Whether cooked leftovers may go into the organic bin is decided by your local waste service.
reis-nudeln.pointe: Pasta keeps getting bigger in the pipe – just like us after dinner.

mehl-teig.name: Flour & dough
mehl-teig.kanal: Flour and water make paste. Dough sticks firmly in pipes.
mehl-teig.pointe: Paste is great for crafts – not for sewer pipes.

nudelwasser.name: Pasta & cooking water
nudelwasser.kanal: Cooking water without fat can go down the sink. Catch the pasta in a sieve first.
nudelwasser.pointe: Water away – but the pasta stays in the sieve!

spuelwasser.name: Washing-up water
spuelwasser.kanal: Washing-up water is normal wastewater. Wipe greasy pans with kitchen paper first, then less fat ends up in the pipe.
spuelwasser.pointe: Wipe the pan first, then wash – the sewer says thanks.

getraenkereste.name: Leftover drinks
getraenkereste.kanal: You can pour leftovers from a glass or cup down the sink.
getraenkereste.hinweis: Empty bottles go to the glass container or back to the shop (deposit).
getraenkereste.pointe: A sip for the sewer is fine – a whole barrel is not.

milch.name: Milk & dairy
milch.kanal: A small drop of milk is no problem. But large amounts put a heavy load on the treatment plant, because bacteria need a lot of oxygen to break it down.
milch.wohinHinweis: Leftovers from a glass: sink. Full cartons or yoghurt pots: general waste, empty pots into the yellow bag.
milch.pointe: Milk makes kids strong – it makes treatment plant bacteria tired.

kaugummi.name: Chewing gum
kaugummi.kanal: Chewing gum is made of a plastic gum base. It never dissolves and sticks to everything.
kaugummi.pointe: Gum sticks everywhere – in the sewer, sadly, forever.

verpackungen.name: Packaging & foil
verpackungen.kanal: Plastic doesn’t break down. It blocks pipes, wraps around pumps and turns into microplastics in rivers.
verpackungen.pointe: Plastic lasts forever – that’s exactly why it doesn’t belong in the toilet.

tabletten.name: Pills & capsules
tabletten.kanal: Treatment plants can’t fully remove many drugs. The residues reach rivers and lakes as micropollutants and harm fish and tiny creatures there.
tabletten.wohinHinweis: Wrap in newspaper or a bag so children and pets can’t get at them. Please check the local rules.
tabletten.pointe: Fish don’t get headaches – they don’t need ibuprofen.

fluessige-medikamente.name: Cough syrup & drops
fluessige-medikamente.kanal: Liquid medicines also contain active ingredients that the treatment plant can’t completely filter out.
fluessige-medikamente.wohinHinweis: Put in the general waste with bottle and cap – do not pour away.
fluessige-medikamente.pointe: The river doesn’t have a cough.

salben.name: Ointments & pain gel
salben.kanal: The painkiller diclofenac is a well-known micropollutant. It is hardly broken down at treatment plants and can damage fish kidneys.
salben.hinweis: After applying, first wipe your hands with a tissue, then wash them – that way less gets into the wastewater.
salben.pointe: Fish don’t pull muscles – diclofenac doesn’t help them.

antibiotika.name: Antibiotics
antibiotika.kanal: Antibiotics in wastewater can help bacteria become resistant. Then the medicines work less well for people.
antibiotika.pointe: Antibiotics in the sewer are a training camp for superbugs.

hormone.name: Hormone products (e.g. the pill)
hormone.kanal: Even tiny amounts of artificial hormones in water can disturb the reproduction of fish.
hormone.pointe: Fish want to decide for themselves whether to start a family.

spritzen.name: Syringes & needles
spritzen.kanal: Needles are dangerous for people working at pumping stations and treatment plants – they can prick themselves and get infected.
spritzen.wohinHinweis: Put in the general waste in a puncture-proof, closed container (e.g. an empty plastic bottle).
spritzen.pointe: Ouch! Nobody wants that at work.

thermometer.name: Mercury thermometer
thermometer.kanal: Mercury is a toxic heavy metal. It builds up in fish – and so in our food.
thermometer.hinweis: Digital thermometers belong with electrical waste or battery collection because of the battery.
thermometer.pointe: Mercury has no business in water – unlike fish.

nikotinpflaster.name: Nicotine patches
nikotinpflaster.kanal: Used medicated patches still contain a lot of active ingredient. It is toxic to aquatic life.
nikotinpflaster.hinweis: Fold the sticky sides together and put in the general waste.
nikotinpflaster.pointe: Fish don’t want to smoke either – not even by patch.

vitamine.name: Vitamins & supplements
vitamine.kanal: These tablets don’t belong in wastewater either. The rule is simple: no medicine and no tablets down the toilet.
vitamine.pointe: The sewer is healthy enough already.

farbe.name: Wall paint & paint leftovers
farbe.kanal: Paint sticks to pipes and contains binders and additives that burden the treatment plant.
farbe.wohinHinweis: Let water-based paint leftovers dry in an open bucket, then general waste. Liquid or solvent-based paints go to hazardous waste collection.
farbe.pointe: The pipe doesn’t want to be redecorated – at least not like this.

pinsel.name: Washing out brushes
pinsel.kanal: Watercolours from a paint box are no problem. With wall paint: first wipe the brush out thoroughly, then rinse only briefly.
pinsel.hinweis: Never wash brushes with varnish or oil paint in the sink – leftovers with thinner go to hazardous waste collection.
pinsel.pointe: Wipe first, then wash – that way the sewer stays make-up free.

lack-loesungsmittel.name: Varnish, thinner & solvents
lack-loesungsmittel.kanal: Solvents can form dangerous, explosive fumes in the sewer. They poison the bacteria that clean the water at the treatment plant.
lack-loesungsmittel.pointe: An explosive mood is great at parties – not in the sewer.

motoroel.name: Engine oil & used oil
motoroel.kanal: Even small amounts of oil can pollute huge amounts of water. Oil forms films on the water and harms plants and animals.
motoroel.wohinHinweis: Anyone who sells engine oil must take back used oil. Keep the receipt!
motoroel.pointe: Engine oil belongs in the engine – not in the river.

benzin.name: Petrol & diesel
benzin.kanal: Petrol fumes can collect in the sewer and explode. That is life-threatening – also for people working in the sewer.
benzin.pointe: There’s enough going on in the sewer – nobody needs fireworks.

frostschutz.name: Antifreeze & coolant
frostschutz.kanal: These liquids are toxic to people, animals and the bacteria at the treatment plant.
frostschutz.pointe: Antifreeze in the sewer? The wastewater won’t freeze – promise.

pflanzenschutz.name: Pesticides & weed killer
pflanzenschutz.kanal: Pesticides are made to kill living things. In water they harm insects, fish and plants.
pflanzenschutz.hinweis: Don’t spray the leftovers on the driveway either – the rain washes them straight into the water.
pflanzenschutz.pointe: The river has no weeds – it has fish.

rohrreiniger.name: Chemical drain cleaner
rohrreiniger.kanal: Drain cleaners are highly corrosive. They can damage seals and plastic pipes and burden the treatment plant. Often they don’t even help.
rohrreiniger.hinweis: Better try a plunger or a drain snake first. Leftovers and old packs go to hazardous waste collection.
rohrreiniger.pointe: A plunger costs little and doesn’t burn – a superhero without a cape.

putzmittel.name: Cleaning products & toilet cleaner
putzmittel.kanal: Normal cleaning according to the instructions is fine. But more doesn’t help more: too much cleaner burdens the treatment plant for nothing.
putzmittel.hinweis: Don’t pour away leftovers or full bottles. Empty bottles go into the yellow bag.
putzmittel.pointe: A squirt makes it clean – not half the bottle.

chlorreiniger.name: Chlorine cleaner
chlorreiniger.kanal: Chlorine kills not only germs in the bathroom but also the useful bacteria at the treatment plant. Use sparingly and only when really needed.
chlorreiniger.hinweis: Never mix with acidic cleaners (e.g. descaler) – this creates toxic chlorine gas!
chlorreiniger.pointe: A clean toilet doesn’t need a chemistry lab.

entkalker.name: Descaler
entkalker.kanal: Used according to the instructions, the spent solution can go down the drain. Leftovers and full packs cannot.
entkalker.pointe: Limescale gone, sewer fine – as long as you don’t overdo it.

desinfektionsmittel.name: Disinfectant
desinfektionsmittel.kanal: A normal household rarely needs disinfectant. Larger amounts harm the bacteria at the treatment plant.
desinfektionsmittel.hinweis: Leftovers and full bottles go to hazardous waste collection.
desinfektionsmittel.pointe: The treatment plant bacteria are the good guys – please don’t disinfect them away.

fotochemie.name: Photo & lab chemicals
fotochemie.kanal: Chemicals can attack pipes, form dangerous gases and disrupt the treatment plant.

batterien.name: Batteries
batterien.kanal: Batteries contain heavy metals and chemicals. Lithium batteries can even catch fire.
batterien.hinweis: Collection boxes are in almost every supermarket and drugstore.
batterien.pointe: Batteries give power – but no good energy in the sewer.

zement-gips.name: Cement, plaster & tile adhesive
zement-gips.kanal: Cement and plaster set rock-hard in the pipe. Then a milling robot has to cut the pipe free again – that’s expensive.
zement-gips.wohinHinweis: Clean buckets and tools outdoors in a bucket of water, let it settle, put the solid residue in the general waste. Larger amounts go to the recycling centre.
zement-gips.pointe: Pour cement down the pipe and you’re setting your future in stone – and the sewer’s.

silikon.name: Silicone & expanding foam
silikon.kanal: Silicone and foam harden and are made of plastic. They stay stuck in the pipe.
silikon.wohinHinweis: Empty, hardened cartridges: general waste. Full cans of foam: hazardous waste collection.
silikon.pointe: Seals joints – and sadly pipes too.

katzenstreu.name: Cat litter
katzenstreu.kanal: Clumping litter sets like concrete with water. Even “flushable” litter settles in pipes. Cat poo can also contain pathogens.
katzenstreu.hinweis: Please don’t flush plant-based litter either – many waste services don’t want it in the organic bin either.
katzenstreu.pointe: The cat uses the litter tray – the litter tray doesn’t use the toilet.

hundekot.name: Dog poo (in a bag)
hundekot.kanal: The bags don’t break down – not even the “compostable” ones fast enough. They get wrapped up in pumps and pipes.
hundekot.pointe: The dog did its job – the bag goes in the bin.

kleintierstreu.name: Small pet bedding & hay
kleintierstreu.kanal: Bedding and hay swell up and block pipes.
kleintierstreu.wohinHinweis: Plant-based bedding may go into the organic bin depending on your waste service – please check locally.
kleintierstreu.pointe: The hamster builds a nest – please don’t let the pipe do the same.

tote-fische.name: Dead fish
tote-fische.kanal: A dead fish can carry pathogens. It doesn’t belong in the toilet – even if films often show it that way.
tote-fische.hinweis: Small animals can often be buried in your own garden. Never release or flush live fish!
tote-fische.pointe: No, Goldie won’t swim back to the sea. The toilet leads to the treatment plant.

aquarienwasser.name: Aquarium water
aquarienwasser.kanal: Water from a water change can go down the toilet – without gravel, plants and fish.
aquarienwasser.hinweis: Tip: aquarium water is a great fertiliser for house plants.
aquarienwasser.pointe: The water can go – Nemo stays.

tierhaare.name: Pet hair
tierhaare.kanal: Pet hair mats just like human hair – usually in larger amounts.
tierhaare.hinweis: Put a strainer in the drain after bathing the dog.
tierhaare.pointe: Fur belongs on the dog – not in the pipe.

tiermedikamente.name: Flea treatments & pet medicines
tiermedikamente.kanal: Flea and tick treatments contain insecticides. Even tiny amounts harm aquatic insects in streams and rivers.
tiermedikamente.hinweis: Don’t bathe freshly treated dogs for a few days or let them jump into streams.
tiermedikamente.pointe: Against fleas – but sadly also against dragonfly larvae.

vogelsand.name: Bird sand
vogelsand.kanal: Sand settles in pipes and the sewer and has to be flushed out with a lot of effort.

zigaretten.name: Cigarette butts
zigaretten.kanal: Cigarette filters are plastic and full of toxins like nicotine. The toxins dissolve in water and harm fish and tiny creatures.
zigaretten.gully: A butt in the street drain ends up straight in the stream – without any treatment!
zigaretten.hinweis: E-cigarettes go to electrical or battery collection because of the battery.
zigaretten.pointe: Fish are non-smokers. All of them.

autowaesche.name: Car-wash water
autowaesche.kanal: Washing a car loosens oil, brake dust and heavy metals. Through the rainwater sewer it flows untreated into the nearest water.
autowaesche.gully: Washing on the street or driveway means: the dirty water runs into the drain and straight into the stream.
autowaesche.pointe: Your car shines – sadly the stream doesn’t.

wischwasser.name: Mop water
wischwasser.kanal: Mop water can go down the toilet or the sink – then it goes to the treatment plant.
wischwasser.gully: Never tip it into the street drain! That leads straight into the stream.
wischwasser.pointe: Toilet yes, street drain no – even the mop remembers that.

laub.name: Leaves & grass cuttings
laub.kanal: Leaves block street drains. In heavy rain the water can’t drain away – the street turns into a lake.
laub.gully: Don’t sweep leaves into the drain and keep the drains in front of your house clear.
laub.pointe: In autumn the street drain is the leaves’ favourite place. Sadly.

erde-sand.name: Potting soil, sand & gravel
erde-sand.kanal: Soil and sand settle in the sewer and narrow the pipes. At the treatment plant they have to be removed in the grit chamber.

asche.name: Ash & charcoal
asche.kanal: Ash forms deposits in the sewer. Barbecue ash can also contain pollutants.
asche.hinweis: Only put completely cooled ash in the bin – otherwise it can catch fire!
asche.pointe: Ashes to ashes – but please into the bin.

kerzenwachs.name: Candle wax
kerzenwachs.kanal: Liquid wax hardens immediately in the cold pipe – like fat, only worse.
kerzenwachs.hinweis: Aluminium tealight cups go into the yellow bag.
kerzenwachs.pointe: Romantic on the table, rock-hard in the pipe.

textilien.name: Socks, tights & textiles
textilien.kanal: Fabrics don’t break down and wrap around pump impellers. Nylon tights are almost untearable.
textilien.pointe: The missing sock isn’t in the toilet – and that’s how it should stay.

lappen.name: Cleaning cloths & sponges
lappen.kanal: Cloths and microfibre cloths are indestructible. At the pumping station they turn into thick ropes.
lappen.pointe: Top for cleaning, a flop at the pumping station.

handschuhe.name: Disposable gloves & masks
handschuhe.kanal: Rubber, latex and fleece don’t break down. They get caught in pumps and screens.

spielzeug.name: Toys
spielzeug.kanal: Toys usually get stuck in your own pipe. Then only a drain cleaning service can help.
spielzeug.hinweis: Better give away whole toys. Broken electronic toys go to electrical waste.
spielzeug.pointe: The rubber duck wants a bath – but in the tub, not in the sewer.

pflanzenreste.name: Cut flowers & house plants
pflanzenreste.kanal: Stems and leaves get caught in pipes and rot there.
pflanzenreste.hinweis: The flower water itself can go down the sink.
pflanzenreste.pointe: Flowers belong on the compost – not at the bottom of the sewer.

haarfaerbemittel.name: Hair dye leftovers
haarfaerbemittel.kanal: When rinsing your hair, a little dye in the wastewater can’t be avoided. But mixed, leftover dye contains many chemicals and doesn’t belong in the water.
haarfaerbemittel.wohinHinweis: Let small leftovers dry and put them in the general waste. Full packs go to hazardous waste collection.
haarfaerbemittel.pointe: New hair colour for you – not for the river.

sonnencreme.name: Sunscreen & body lotion
sonnencreme.kanal: Don’t flush expired creams down the toilet. They contain fats, UV filters and other substances the treatment plant can’t fully remove.
sonnencreme.hinweis: Empty tubes and bottles go into the yellow bag, leftovers with packaging into general waste.
sonnencreme.pointe: The sewer doesn’t need sun protection – the sun doesn’t shine down there.

zahnbuerste.name: Toothbrush
zahnbuerste.kanal: If a toothbrush falls into the toilet, please fish it out! It gets stuck in the pipe and catches everything else.
zahnbuerste.hinweis: Electric toothbrushes go to electrical waste.
zahnbuerste.pointe: The toothbrush cleans teeth – the pipe doesn’t clean it.

lebende-tiere.name: Live animals
lebende-tiere.kanal: Animals never belong in the toilet – that is animal cruelty. Released aquarium animals can also push out native species.
lebende-tiere.wohinHinweis: Ask a pet shop, animal shelter or animal welfare group – they’ll help. Simply carry a spider outside with a glass and paper.
lebende-tiere.pointe: The toilet isn’t a water slide to adventure land.

gummiband.name: Rubber bands & hair ties
gummiband.kanal: Rubber bands are perfect anchors: hair and wipes get caught on them and form ropes.
gummiband.pointe: Plaits look great on your head – not at the pumping station.

papier-pappe.name: Newspaper, cardboard & paper
papier-pappe.kanal: Only toilet paper breaks down quickly. Newspaper, napkins and cardboard are much stronger and block the pipe.
papier-pappe.wohinHinweis: Clean paper and cardboard into paper recycling, used napkins into general waste.
papier-pappe.pointe: Out of toilet paper? Better ask the neighbours than reach for the newspaper.
